reading.body:
Browser-use leads this category with over 111,000 stars, nearly double the next project, which suggests browser automation has attracted more open-source interest than coding assistance despite coding agents being the older use case.

The five projects together hold roughly 288,000 stars, all under permissive licences, either Apache-2.0 or MIT. Permissive licencing matters here because it allows commercial products to be built on top without legal friction, which accelerates adoption into professional developer tooling. All five repositories received commits as recently as September 2026, so none of these projects are dormant.

The data covers only GitHub star counts, licences, and activity dates. Stars reflect developer attention, not deployment volume or inference cost. Because coding and browser agents run queries against large models, their compute demand scales with usage, but nothing in this data quantifies how much inference each project drives or what power that inference consumes. The data also covers only five repositories, and the field may have relevant projects hosted elsewhere or kept proprietary.
